proof:
This is the product of c3e79bc0190bfda3. Its affine mismatch function at $v$ is exactly $-(2v-\mathbf1)\cdot(z-v)$, an integer at least one at any other binary base. The source chooses mismatch coefficient one, already sufficient to exclude other fibers since $\lambda_j\le1$ and $1/(d+1)>0$. At $v$ it gives the same canonical cap, of fraction $\Gamma_d$, and the $d+1$ caps cover $T$ because the barycentric coordinates sum to one. Thus every mark is in a cap of mass $\Gamma_d/N$. By the own centroid cap bound used in c3e79bc0190bfda3, every containing halfspace captures at least this much at $(v,g)$; this also includes pure-base cuts, which retain the full own fiber. The canonical cap attains equality there, so the entire menu is critical.

The capture function is $\Gamma_d\mathbf1_{\{z=v\}}$, so the covariance is exactly $\Gamma_dp_v(v-m)$. Subtract the column $-m$ from each of the other raw columns to get $e_1,\ldots,e_{n-1}$; expansion gives absolute determinant $m_n$, positive because the posterior gives weight to sites with $z_n=1$. This includes $n=1$ with no subtraction. The positive scalar factors give the stated determinant; at the uniform prior $m_n=1/2$. Finite Gaussian parameters keep all posterior weights positive, so adaptive-gaussian-active-cap-freezing gives $A=0$ almost everywhere if all the active bounds are preserved. In fact the selected $n$ caps already suffice. The original weights equal $2^{-n}$, so this example alone does not address a rule that stops on a heavy fiber.
statement:
Let $n,d\ge1$, $P=\{0,1\}^n$, $N=2^n$, and put the same $d$-simplex $T$ at each base. Write $\lambda_j$ for its barycentric coordinates, $g$ for its centroid, and $\Gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$. Under the original normalized mixed volume, the actual caps
$$
H_{v,j}=\{\lambda_j(X)+(2v-\mathbf1)\cdot(z-v)\ge1/(d+1)\}
$$
have mass $\Gamma_d/N$, jointly cover the actual mixed set, and each attains the depth at its own centroid $(v,g)$. The global original maximal depth equals $\Gamma_d/N$. At every positive posterior $p$ these caps have covariance vectors $\Gamma_d p_v(v-m)$ spanning $\mathbb R^n$. In particular the absolute determinant for one cap at each of $v_0=0,v_1=e_1,\ldots,v_{n-1}=e_{n-1}$ is $\Gamma_d^n m_n\prod_{j=0}^{n-1}p_{v_j}$, initially $\Gamma_d^n/(2N^n)$. An existing adaptive Gaussian process that preserves all these initially tight bounds has $A_t=0$ almost everywhere.
title: A sharp actual simplex-product cover freezes adaptive base covariance
